The 50 best mystery novels of 2026

Page 2 of 5 · Ranks 11–20 · How we ranked them

11. The Night Ferry by Dana Almeida

An overnight ferry crossing becomes a locked-room puzzle when a passenger vanishes between ports. Almeida's pacing is immaculate, and the final chapter's reveal recontextualizes three separate set pieces without cheating. A masterclass in misdirection.

12. Cold Harbour Lane by Rowan Beck

A cold-case podcaster moves next door to the family she suspects. Beck plays the ethics of true-crime obsession without letting the meta-commentary swamp the mystery. The procedural detail is unusually accurate.

13. The Archivist's Daughter by Lucia Ferreira

In 1974 Lisbon, an archivist's daughter decodes her late father's cataloging system to find documents the regime wants destroyed. Historical mystery at its finest — dense, humane, and impossible to put down.

14. Smoke on the Water by Tomas Lindqvist

A wildfire evacuation unearths a body that cannot be the one already buried in the town cemetery. Lindqvist keeps a dozen suspects vivid while the fire closes in. The Scandinavian setting is a character itself.

15. The Last Train from Tallinn by Kaire Tamm

1939: a courier with forged papers shares a compartment with the man hired to intercept her. Tamm sustains unbearable tension across 300 pages with barely a raised voice. Quietly devastating.
